## Packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
```

## Loading in Data

```{r}
getwd()
tree_height_complete <- read_csv("data/tree_height_analysis.csv")
fluxes_filtered <- read_csv("data/fluxes_filtered.csv")
tree_specs <- read_excel("data/data_raw/DBH and circumference measurements_up tree.xlsx", sheet="raw data")
```

```{r}
# Adding back in the height_cm variable:

# Assigning heights to temporary tibble
heights_cm <- tibble(
  height = c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e"),
  height_cm = c(45, 95, 145, 195, 345))
heights_cm

# Adding a "height" column, based on the a/b/c/d/e attached to tree_id
fluxes_filtered <- fluxes_filtered |> 
  mutate(
    tree_num = str_extract(tree_id, "^[0-9]{4}"),
    height   = str_extract(tree_id, "[a-zA-Z]$"),
    height   = ifelse(is.na(height), "a", height)
  )

# Joining the temporary tibble to the new dataframe; all_height
all_height <- fluxes_filtered |> 
  filter(surface=="stem") |> 
  left_join(heights_cm, by = "height")
```

## Finding the median multiplier (to be used for all other calculations where height wasn't measured)

```{r}
# Calculating the median and mean of the multiplier value. Note: the 'na.rm = T' indicates that we are only interested in the non-NA, or real, values of the multiplier - this is important because the multiplier was only calculated at one of the heights (45 cm), so every other height in this dataset is by default going to have a value of NA for the multipler column we're interested in.

tree_height_complete |> 
  summarize(median_multiplier=median(multiplier_a, na.rm=T), 
            mean_multiplier=mean(multiplier_a, na.rm=T))

# Histogram. Notice, binwdith = 0.3, and this is a stacked histogram to see the distributions of the multiplier at every tree at once.

ggplot(tree_height_complete,
       aes(x = multiplier_a, fill = factor(tree_num))) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.3, color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Tree") +
  labs(x = "Multiplier A", 
       y = "Count",
       title = "Stacked Histogram of Multiplier A Distribution by Tree") +
  theme_minimal()

# Unstacked histogram: in geom_histogram() function, 'position = "identity"' indicates to separately graph each of the trees; 'alpha = 0.5' indicates transparency of colors

ggplot(tree_height_complete,
       aes(x = multiplier_a, fill = factor(tree_num))) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.3,
                 position = "identity",
                 alpha = 0.5,
                 color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Tree") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Multiplier A by Tree",
       x = "Multiplier A",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The "multiplier" is the number that we're prepared to use to infer the total emission of a given tree after only measuring the surface area of a tree from 0-70cm, and the flux rate at 45 cm. The median multiplier is 1.45, while the mean multiplier is 2.15. Given that there was a right skew on a few outliers in the data, we will use the median as the best approximation of center of our data (see distribution on histograms).

```{r}
# Note: NAs are as follows:
# Tree 1616, March 2014
# Tree 1616, June 2014
# Tree 1614, June 2014


given_height_tree_total_methane <- tree_height_complete |> 
  group_by(month, year, tree_num) |> 
  filter(height_cm==45) |> 
  select(tree_num, month, year, flux, total_tree_flux) |> 
  rename(flux_45cm = flux)
```

## Tree Specs for all trees

```{r}
# Renaming all columns in tree_spec data

# Important note: I am assuming the circumference is the best measurement. In the raw data, circumference and diameter disagreed by a small margin on the trees.

tree_specs <- tree_specs |> 
  rename(tree_num=Tree) |> 
  rename(circum_bh_cm=`circumference BH`) |> 
  rename(circum_30cm=`circumference 30cm`) |> 
  rename(ground_area_circum_cm=`ground area (circumference)`) |> 
  select(tree_num, circum_bh_cm, circum_30cm, ground_area_circum_cm)
  
```

```{r}
# This function  returns the bark surface area, in m^2, of the bottom 0-70 cm of a trunk

# Inputs:
#   C30   = trunk circumference at 30 cm height (cm)
#   CBH   = trunk circumference at breast height (cm)
#   h30   = height C30 was measured (default 30 cm)
#   hBH   = height BH was measured (default 130 cm)
#   h_top = top of the section we want (default 70 cm)

area_0_70 <- function(C30, CBH, h30 = 30, hBH = 130, h_top = 70) {
  
  # Estimate circumference at 70 cm by straight-line interpolation between
  # the two measured points. (CBH - C30) is the total change in circumference
  # over the (hBH - h30) = 100 cm gap. (h_top - h30)/(hBH - h30) = 0.4 is how
  # far up that gap 70 cm sits, so we add 40% of the change to C30
  
  C70 <- C30 + (CBH - C30) * (h_top - h30) / (hBH - h30)
  
  # Convert circumference to radius (C = 2*pi*r)
  
  r30 <- C30 / (2 * pi)
  r70 <- C70 / (2 * pi)
  
  # Vertical height of the 30-70 cm section (40 cm)
  sect <- h_top - h30
  
  # Slant height of the tapered section found with Pythagorean theorem from the vertical height and the drop in radius
  slant <- sqrt(sect^2 + (r30 - r70)^2)
  
  # 0-30 cm: no measurement below 30 cm, so assume a straight cylinder at the 30 cm circumference. Cylinder side area = circumference x height
  base  <- C30 * h30
  
  # 30-70 cm: a truncated cone (frustum). Its side area is the average of the top and bottom circumferences x the slant height
  upper <- (C30 + C70) / 2 * slant
  
  # Add the two pieces (cm^2) and convert to m^2 (100 cm x 100 cm = 10,000)
  (base + upper) / 10000
}

# Add a new column to tree_specs by running the function on every row, feeding it each tree's circumference at 30 cm and at breast height
tree_specs <- tree_specs |>
  mutate(surface_area_0_70_m2 = area_0_70(circum_30cm, circum_bh_cm))



tree_specs |> select(tree_num, circum_30cm, circum_bh_cm, surface_area_0_70_m2)
```

```{r}
# Averaging fluxes per tree
flux45 <- all_height |>
  filter(height_cm == 45) |>
  group_by(tree_num, year, month) |>
  mutate(tree_num=as.numeric(tree_num)) |> 
  summarise(flux_45cm = mean(flux, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

unique(flux45$tree_num)
```

```{r}
# Assigning the trees
single_trees <- c(1604, 1605, 1606, 1609, 1610, 1611, 1612, 1615, 1617)
# Assigning the multiplier
mult_med <- 1.45

# This function will filter down to single_trees, and then will join the tree_specs with surface area measurements by the tree_num. From there, I applied the equation of multiplying the flux rate by the surface area by the multiplier to estimate the total flux of each tree.

tree_flux <- flux45 |>
  filter(tree_num %in% single_trees) |>
  left_join(tree_specs |> select(tree_num, surface_area_0_70_m2),
            by = "tree_num") |>
  mutate(flux_0_70_umol_s       = surface_area_0_70_m2 * flux_45cm,
         total_tree_flux_umol_s = flux_0_70_umol_s * mult_med)

# Adding a date variable
tree_flux$date <- as.Date(paste(tree_flux$month, "1", tree_flux$year), format = "%B %d %Y")
```

```{r}
ggplot(tree_flux, aes(x=date, y= total_tree_flux_umol_s, color=tree_num))+
  geom_point()+
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
avg_total_tree <- tree_flux |> 
  dplyr::group_by(month) |> 
  summarize(mean_tree_emission = mean(total_tree_flux_umol_s),
            median_tree_emission = median(total_tree_flux_umol_s),
            iqr_tree_emission = IQR(total_tree_flux_umol_s)
  )
```

## Adding in Breast Height

```{r}
# calculating diameter (from circumference used)
tree_specs <- tree_specs |>
  mutate(dbh_cm = circum_bh_cm / pi)

# joining the data
tree_flux <- tree_flux |>
  left_join(tree_specs |> select(tree_num, dbh_cm), by = "tree_num")

tree_height_complete <- tree_height_complete |>
  left_join(tree_specs |> select(tree_num, dbh_cm), by = "tree_num")
```

## Extrapolating trees 1601, 1603, 1607, 1608, and 1613

```{r}
target_trees <- c(1601, 1603, 1607, 1608, 1613)
mult_med <- 1.45

# Median 45 cm flux per m^2 for each month (same as before)
monthly_flux <- flux45 |>
  group_by(year, month) |>
  summarise(median_flux_45cm = median(flux_45cm, na.rm = TRUE),
            q25 = quantile(flux_45cm, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            q75 = quantile(flux_45cm, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_trees = n(),
            .groups = "drop")

# A small function that does the calculation for ONE tree
estimate_one_tree <- function(tree_id) {
  this_tree <- tree_specs |> filter(tree_num == tree_id)
  area <- this_tree$surface_area_0_70_m2
  dbh  <- this_tree$dbh_cm
  
  monthly_flux |>
    mutate(
      tree_num               = tree_id,
      dbh_cm                 = dbh,
      surface_area_0_70_m2   = area,
      flux_0_70_umol_s       = area * median_flux_45cm,
      total_tree_flux_umol_s = flux_0_70_umol_s * mult_med,
      total_low              = area * q25 * mult_med,
      total_high             = area * q75 * mult_med
    )
}

# Run it for each target tree and stack the results
est_unmeasured <- bind_rows(lapply(target_trees, estimate_one_tree))
```

## Estimating total methane emission of ALL trees

```{r}
# 25th and 75th percentile multipliers (from all profiled trees)
mult_q <- quantile(tree_height_complete$multiplier_a, c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)

tree_flux <- tree_flux |>
  mutate(
    total_low  = flux_0_70_umol_s * mult_q[[1]],
    total_high = flux_0_70_umol_s * mult_q[[2]]
  )

profiled <- tree_height_complete |> 
  ungroup() |>
  distinct(tree_num, year, month, total_tree_flux) |>
  transmute(tree_num, year, month,
            total_tree_flux_umol_s = total_tree_flux,
            total_low  = total_tree_flux,
            total_high = total_tree_flux,
            source = "measured profile")

single <- tree_flux |>
  transmute(tree_num, year, month, total_tree_flux_umol_s,
            total_low, total_high,
            source = "single chamber x 1.45")

unmeasured <- est_unmeasured |>
  transmute(tree_num, year, month, total_tree_flux_umol_s,
            total_low, total_high,
            source = "estimated from median flux")

all_est <- bind_rows(profiled, single, unmeasured)
```

```{r}
tree_flux_estimates <- all_est |> 
  group_by(month, year) |> 
  summarise(estimated_emission_tree = sum(total_tree_flux_umol_s), .groups = "drop")
```

## Estimating soil

```{r}
# Start with getting the total area of the soil in the 20m x 20m plot
# We need to subtract the basal area of the 17 trees.

tree_basal_area <- tree_specs |> 
  # Conversion from cm2 to m2
  mutate(ground_area_circum_m2=ground_area_circum_cm/10000) |> 
  select(tree_num, ground_area_circum_m2)

total_tree_area<- sum(tree_basal_area$ground_area_circum_m2, na.rm=T)
# 5.396 m2

total_area<-20*20
# 400 m2

total_soil_area<-total_area-total_tree_area
total_soil_area
# 394.6 m2
```

```{r}
# Grabbing the methane soil fluxes by month
soil_fluxes <- fluxes_filtered |> 
  filter(surface=="soil") |> 
  select(month, year, tree_num, surface, flux)

# Getting median values
# Adding in the area for equations, calculating area*flux
soil_flux_medians <- soil_fluxes |> 
  group_by(month, year) |> 
  summarise(median_flux = median(flux), n = n()) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(total_soil_area = total_soil_area)

# Estimates for soil:
soil_flux_estimates <- soil_flux_medians |> 
  group_by(month, year) |> 
  mutate(estimated_emission_soil=median_flux*total_soil_area)
```

```{r}
# All together
flux_estimates <- full_join(soil_flux_estimates, tree_flux_estimates,
                            by = c("month", "year")) |> 
  select(month, year, estimated_emission_tree, estimated_emission_soil)


# Data transformation to get categories
flux_long <- flux_estimates |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(estimated_emission_tree, estimated_emission_soil),
               names_to = "source",
               values_to = "emission") |> 
  mutate(source = recode(source,
                         estimated_emission_tree = "Tree",
                         estimated_emission_soil = "Soil"),
         month = factor(month, levels = month.name))

ggplot(flux_long, aes(x = month, y = emission, colour = source)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Month",
       y = "Estimated emission (mu mol/s)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
